# PART 1 — UNIVERSAL

> **Applicability by project type (universal pack):** Part 1 is written for
> service-shaped systems. For other types, apply the spirit, not the letter:
> **cli / library** — "Controllers" = command handlers / public API surface
> (delegate only still applies); hexagonal = keep core logic free of I/O and
> framework imports; global error handler = single top-level error path with
> meaningful exit codes. **data-ml / batch** — "Controllers" = pipeline entry
> points; contract tests = schema validation on every external dataset.
> **frontend / mobile** — "Controllers" = components (no business logic in
> components); ports = service/API layer. Testing, PR, Logging, Git, and
> Definition of Done rules apply unchanged to every type.

## Architecture

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Pattern | Hexagonal — domain isolated from infrastructure |
| External | Port interfaces only — never direct calls |
| Start | Mock-first before real adapter |
| Class | One responsibility — split if doing two things |

## Code Quality

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Controllers | Delegate only — zero business logic |
| Injection | Interface — never concrete class |
| Config | Env vars only — no hardcoded values |
| Dead code | Delete — never comment out |

## PR Rules

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Workflow mode | {from manifest.workflow_mode} — github: PR + CI checks; local: agent runs checks, human says "go" |
| Max lines | {from manifest.pr_rules.max_lines_per_pr} |
| Max files | {from manifest.pr_rules.max_files_per_pr} |
| Tests | Same PR/task always |
| Class max | 200 lines — split before commit |
| Over limit | Estimate → SPLIT A/B/C → confirm → one at a time |

## Testing

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Style | Set in manifest.testing_style: paired (default) · tdd · bdd |
| Pairing | Every class/component has a test — same PR, never deferred |
| Unit | Mock all external dependencies |
| Naming | should_{expected}_when_{condition} |
| Coverage | As specified in tech stack (Part 2) |
| Contract | Consumer-driven contract tests (Pact / schema validation) for every outbound integration — in same PR as the adapter |

## Logging

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Format | Structured JSON always |
| PII | Never in any log at any level |
| Trace | Correlation/trace ID on every line |
| Level | INFO=business WARN=recoverable ERROR=failure |

## Error Handling

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Exceptions | All extend base application exception |
| Handler | Single global handler |
| Response | errorCode + message + timestamp — no stack trace |

## Git

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | feature/{n} fix/{n} chore/{n} |
| Commit | {type}({scope}): {description} |
| PR ref | Every PR references TASK-NNN or CHG-NNN |
| Merge | No direct commits to main or develop |

## Definition of Done

| Gate | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Tests green | All unit + integration tests pass in CI |
| Coverage met | Meets coverage gate defined in Part 2 Tech Stack |
| Linting clean | Zero linting errors (tool set in Part 2) |
| Security scan clean | No new HIGH/CRITICAL findings (OWASP dependency check or equivalent) |
| Pre-review passed | /pre-review completed; selected findings addressed |
| No open TODOs | No `TODO` / `FIXME` / `HACK` comments in committed code |
| PR description complete | References TASK-NNN; summarises change; lists test evidence |
| Paired test exists | Every class/component changed has a test in the same PR |

## Containerization (OPS-7)

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Base image | `-alpine` (or distroless) always — pin exact version |
| User | Non-root: dedicated `appuser` in every image |
| Secrets | `.env` file — never in compose or Dockerfile |
| Build | Multi-stage — no build tooling in the runtime image |
| Health | `healthcheck` defined on every service |
| Volumes | Named volumes for all persistent data |
| Networks | Single bridge network per stack |
| Depends | `condition: service_healthy` — not just `depends_on` |

See .specify/templates/docker-config-template.md for ready-to-use
docker-compose.yml, Dockerfile, and .env.example matching these rules.

If Tech Stack → Orchestration = Kubernetes, see
.specify/templates/k8s-manifest-template.md for Deployment, Service,
HPA, NetworkPolicy, ConfigMap, and Secret manifests matching the same
rules — used instead of docker-compose.yml for cluster deployment.

## Environments

| Environment | Purpose | Config Source | Secrets Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| local-dev | Developer machine | application-local.yml / .env | .env (gitignored) |
| mock | Agent testing with mock adapters | application-mock.yml | .env (gitignored) |
| staging | Pre-production integration testing | Config server / env vars | Vault / secrets manager |
| production | Live traffic | Config server / env vars | Vault / secrets manager |

**Rules:**
- Staging must mirror production configuration (same image, same config source, different secrets)
- Never promote an image that has not passed staging
- Local-dev must run with `docker-compose up` from a clean checkout (no manual setup steps)
- Feature flags (if used): staging = production values by default; only override explicitly

## SDD Workflow

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Order | SPECIFY→[GATE-1]→VALIDATE→ANALYZE→CLARIFY→PLAN→TASK→IMPLEMENT→RELEASE |
| Gates | GATE-1 before VALIDATE · VALIDATE before ANALYZE · CLARIFY before PLAN-ARCH · no unresolved [ASSUMPTION-NNN] before PLAN-ARCH (AI-8) · TASK approved before IMPLEMENT · all tasks merged before RELEASE |
| Change | Update context.md first — never code first |

## Tech Stack

| Concern | Choice | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Language | TypeScript 5.6 | `strict: true`; no implicit `any` |
| Framework | Express 4.19 on Node.js 20 LTS | Thin routers; all logic in services |
| Build Tool | tsc (type-check + emit) | `npm run build` |
| API Style | REST / JSON over HTTPS | Resource routes under `/tasks` |
| Messaging/Async | None for this feature | Reminder dispatch is a separate service |
| Serialisation | JSON (`express.json`) | 1 MB body cap |
| Schema | Zod 3.23 | One schema per endpoint; parsed at the edge |
| Data Store | PostgreSQL 16 | Single primary; no read replica at pilot scope |
| Data Cache | None | Revisit only if NFR-001 is missed under load |
| DB Migration | Prisma Migrate | Versioned SQL in `prisma/migrations/` |
| Configuration | Environment variables via dotenv | No hardcoded values anywhere |
| Secrets | Env vars injected by the platform | JWT public key read from env; never committed |
| Resilience | Per-user rate limit (express-rate-limit) | 300 req/min per user |
| Observability | Structured JSON logs to stdout | Platform ships and indexes them |
| Logging | Request-scoped logger with `request_id` | Never log PII; `user_id` hashed (NFR-004) |
| Testing | Jest 29 + Supertest 6 | Unit plus HTTP integration against a real database |
| Coverage Gate | 80% lines on `src/services` and `src/middleware` | Enforced in CI |
| Quality/Security | Semgrep SAST in CI (NFR-003) | OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023) |
| Orchestration | Container image, one stateless process | Horizontally scalable |
| CI/CD | GitHub Actions | Build, test, SAST on every PR |

## Service NFR Baseline

> Filled at `/specify` from `context.md`'s NFR section (if stated) or the
> first feature's `srd.md`. This is the service-wide performance/
> availability floor — every endpoint/operation in every feature meets
> this unless a feature's own `srd.md` explicitly states a stricter or
> different target. Later features reference this row instead of
> restating it; only a genuinely different target gets its own NFR-NNN
> row in that feature's `srd.md`.

| Category | Target | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Performance | p95 ≤ 200 ms at 100 concurrent users | NFR-001; k6 load test in staging |
| Availability | ≥ 99.9% monthly (≤ 43 min downtime) | NFR-002; external uptime monitoring |
| Throughput | 300 requests/min per user sustained | Rate-limit ceiling, not a capacity target |
| Data Retention | Completed tasks purged 90 days after completion | Cron job in a separate service |

## Core Principles

| Principle | Applied As |
|---|---|
| Specification First | No code before spec + TASK approved |
| Test Discipline | Every class tested per manifest.testing_style — same PR, never deferred |
| Traceability | task → story → FR → context — always |
| Tenant Isolation by Construction | Every query is scoped to the caller's `user_id` in the data layer, never by a caller-supplied filter |
| Validate at the Edge | Every request body and query string is parsed by a Zod schema before reaching a service |

## Domain Rules

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Task ownership | A user may read or modify only their own tasks; cross-user access is a 404, never a 403 |
| Title | Required; 1–200 characters after trim |
| Description | Optional; max 2000 characters |
| Due date | Optional; must not be in the past when a task is created |
| Priority | `low` \| `medium` \| `high`; defaults to `medium` |
| Status | `open` \| `in-progress` \| `done`; defaults to `open` |
| Deletion | Soft delete via an archived flag; rows are never hard-deleted by the API |
| Purge | Tasks with status `done` are purged 90 days after completion |
| Pagination | Cursor-based, 20 items per page by default |

## Never Do

| Rule | Reason |
|---|---|
| Trust a `user_id` from the request body or query string | The only authority is the verified JWT subject — anything else is a tenant-isolation hole |
| Return 403 for another user's task | Confirms the row exists; leaks the ID space. Return 404 |
| Log a task title, description, or raw `user_id` | They are user content and PII (NFR-004) |
| Hard-delete a task row | Deletion is an archived flag; purge is a separate scheduled job |
| Logic in controller | separation of concerns |
| Hardcode any value | security + maintainability |
| Skip paired test | quality gate |
| PR over limit without split | reviewability |
| Code before context update | traceability |
